source.title: Diversity of Transformer Layers: One Aspect of Parameter Scaling Laws
source.authors: Hidetaka Kamigaito; Ying Zhang; Jingun Kwon; Katsuhiko Hayashi; Manabu Okumura; Taro Watanabe

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates downstream task accuracy as layer count varies and relates diminishing gains to parameter scaling laws, but it does not fit loss-scaling curves or train runs at different parameter, token, or compute scales.
record.gate_note: The paper measures residual-stream MSE, bias, diversity, and downstream accuracy; it reports layer-count results and layer-sharing comparisons. It does not measure held-out pretraining cross-entropy, fit power laws, or test compute-optimal allocations. Results cited from other work are not recorded.
record.test_reason: The core is a theoretical bias-diversity analysis. Figure 6 (§5.5) compares off-the-shelf models of 1B–14.7B parameters, grouped by layer count (33/57/65/81). It averages downstream accuracy over 8 tasks and reports diminishing, and partly negative, gains as models get deeper and larger. This bears weakly on V6. It does not fit or measure pretraining loss, so V1–V5 and V7 are untested.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The paper is mainly theoretical. It argues that layer diversity drives performance gains from added layers and that these gains are submodular, i.e. diminishing, which it calls consistent with parameter scaling laws. Its empirical check is on off-the-shelf models' downstream accuracy, not on loss.
record.recipe_differences: Uses residual-stream bias/diversity analysis and downstream semantic-task accuracy at layer junctions, rather than fitting held-out language-model loss across trained parameter, token, or compute scales.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported influence of module type on diversity varies by model; MLP layers dominate diversity overall, but the tendency differs across models. Layer-sharing comparisons and layer-count results are also distinct settings.

fits_no_version.finding: MobileLLM layer-sharing checkpoints have lower average accuracy than their non-shared counterparts (125M: 45.6 vs 46.3; 350M: 44.3 vs 46.0). Their diversity is much lower (1.8 vs 12.2; 4.2 vs 15.5).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adding depth by reusing layers at fixed parameter count gives little or no downstream gain, which the authors link to low inter-layer diversity.

fits_no_version.finding: Residual-stream MSE correlates highly with accuracy across tasks. Bias and diversity correlations are moderate and task-dependent (Figure 3).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Layer-wise bias and diversity in the residual stream relate to downstream accuracy, with task-dependent roles.

record.problems: Figure 6 provides no extractable numeric values in the text; the reported layer-count result is averaged across tasks and models with no less than 1B parameters. The experiments use downstream accuracy and residual-stream MSE rather than held-out pretraining cross-entropy, and do not directly test cross-run scaling or extrapolation.
record.rows_left_out: The paper reports task-specific MobileLLM results in Table 1 and per-task, per-model measures in Figures 3, 5, and 7. Those detailed outcomes are not extracted here; the Table 1 averages and Figure 6 aggregate are retained as the most directly relevant layer-sharing and layer-count summaries.

untested.parts: No pretraining loss, no power-law fits in parameters, tokens or compute.
No loss at fixed parameters across shapes. Layer sharing is reported only as task accuracy and residual MSE.
No controlled scale sweep within one model family. No relation of downstream accuracy to pretraining loss. No fitted downstream trend.
No comparison of fits or exponents.

record.verdict_notes: Figure 6 groups different model families by layer count, so depth, size, training data and instruction tuning are all confounded. The V6 evidence is weak and qualitative. Table 1 also reports bias and diversity blocks that are not recorded as rows. The diversity drop under layer sharing is the authors' main explanatory number.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining cross-entropy or power-law fits in parameters, tokens, or compute.
No small-run fits or predictions of larger-run loss.
No fixed-compute allocation experiment or fitted parameter/token trends.
Layer count and layer sharing are examined, but the study does not measure loss at fixed parameter count while varying depth, width, or other architecture details.
No other modalities, repeated-data regimes, fine-tuning, or transfer scaling-law experiments.
The study examines downstream accuracy as layer count varies, not performance across independently trained parameter scales or predictability from pretraining loss.
No comparison of fitted scaling exponents or compute-optimal splits across fitting choices, and no test of curves bending away from fitted power laws.

rows.subject: models with no less than 1B of parameters (average across all tasks)
rows.operation_detail: Averaged downstream accuracy at residual-stream layer junctions as layer size varies.
rows.note: The authors state that the effectiveness of increasing layers decreases and describe performance degradation caused by increasing layers. This is a layer-count analysis, not a sweep of independently trained model sizes.
rows.check: Subject is a pool of different model families (Llama-3.2 1B/3B, Phi-3/3.5, Llama-2, Mistral, Llama-3/3.1, Phi-3-medium, phi-4), base and instruct mixed, grouped by layer count (Table 4). Layer count is a confounded proxy for scale. Values cannot be read from the figure. The text states only that effectiveness decreases and that some degradation occurs.

rows.note: This is residual-stream MSE, not held-out pretraining cross-entropy. The text does not specify the direction of the MSE curve.
rows.check: This MSE is between a one-hot gold label and softmax outputs at residual-stream junctions on classification prompts. It is not held-out pretraining loss.

relationships.condition: Off-the-shelf LLMs of at least 1B parameters, grouped by layer count (33–81), 8 prompted classification tasks, averaged accuracy
relationships.reason: The authors report diminishing returns and some performance degradation as layers/size increase (r1, Figure 6, text only). Downstream gains are not monotone in this heterogeneous cross-family comparison. No numbers are readable, and model family is confounded with size.
relationships.display_finding: Average classification accuracy showed diminishing returns and occasional degradation as depth and size increased, with model family confounding the comparison.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.condition: Models with no less than 1B parameters, averaged across tasks, as layer count varies
reader_labels.reason: The authors report diminishing effectiveness and performance degradation with additional layers, so downstream performance does not uniformly improve in this tested layer-count setting (r1). This is not a direct test across trained model scales.
